speaker: Teacher (place doctrine)
question: Where is the worship-place?
premises: atha prasannahṛdayo yāgasthānaṃ yāyāt — glad-hearted, go to the worship-place.
tatra yatraiva hṛdayaṃ prasādayuktaṃ parameśvarasamāveśayogyaṃ bhavati — where the heart is gladdened, fit for Lord-immersion.
tad eva na anyat lakṣaṇam — that alone, not anything else, is the mark.
uktāv api dhyeyatādātmyam eva kāraṇam — even when stated, meditated-identity alone is the cause.
tad api bhāvaprasādād eva — that too from being-glad alone.
iti nānyat sthānam — thus no other place.
inference: Place = wherever the heart is gladdened; meditated-identity the cause.

option_choices.reason: stated-sense fits meditated-identity frame; absolutive needs same subject

speaker: Teacher (seats)
question: What of seats and mountains?
premises: pīṭhaparvatāgram ityādis tu śāstre sthānoddeśa etatpara eva boddhavyaḥ — seat-mountain-top and the rest in scripture: to be understood as aimed at this place-pointing.

speaker: Teacher (why places help)
question: How do places help?
premises: teṣu teṣu pīṭhādiṣthāneṣu parameśaniyatyā parameśvarāviṣṭānāṃ śaktīnāṃ dehagrahaṇāt — in seats, by Lord's ordainment, entered powers taking body.
āryadeśā iva dhārmikāṇāṃ mlecchadeśā iva adhārmikāṇām — like noble lands for the pious, barbarian lands for the impious.
parvatāgrādeś caikāntatvena vikṣepaparihārāt aikāgryapadatvam — mountain-top teaching: solitude avoids distraction, one-pointed state.
inference: Entered powers + solitude-concentration explain helpful places.

speaker: Teacher (general nyāsa)
question: What first?
premises: tatra yāgagṛhāgre bahir eva sāmānyanyāsaṃ kuryāt — before the worship-house, outside alone, do the general placing.
karayoḥ pūrvaṃ tato dehe — first on hands, then on the body.
inference: General placing: hands then body, outside.

speaker: Teacher (mantras)
question: With what mantras?
premises: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ ity ābhyāṃ śaktiśaktimadvācakābhyāṃ mālinīśabdarāśimantrābhyām — with the two Mālinī-alphabet mantras expressing power and power-bearer.
ekenaiva ādau śaktiḥ tataḥ śaktimān — with each singly: first power, then power-bearer.
muktau pādāgrāc chiro'ntam bhuktau tu sarvo viparyayaḥ — in release foot-to-head; in enjoyment all reversed.
inference: Two mantras; Śakti first; foot-to-head for release, reversed for enjoyment.

speaker: Teacher (Mālinī)
question: What is Mālinī?
premises: mālinī hi bhagavatī mukhyaṃ śāktaṃ rūpam — Mālinī the Goddess is the chief Śākta form.
bījayonisaṃghaṭṭena samastakāmadugham — by seed-womb collision, all-wish-milking.
inference: Chief Śākta form; seed-womb collision grants all wishes.

speaker: Teacher (her name)
question: Why is the name fitting?
premises: anvarthaṃ caitan nāma rudraśaktimālābhir yuktā — fitting is this name: garlanded with Rudra-power garlands.
phaleṣu puṣpitā — flowering in fruits.
saṃsāraśiśirasaṃhāranādabhramarī — the winter-dissolving-sound bee.
siddhimokṣadhāriṇī — holding attainment-release.
dānādānaśaktiyuktā — endowed with giving-taking power.
iti ralayor ekatvasmṛteḥ — since ra and la are held one.
inference: Seven epithets unfold the name; ra=la identity noted.

speaker: Teacher (Mālinī's power)
question: What does her nyāsa do?
premises: ata eva hi bhraṣṭavidhir api mantra etannyāsāt pūrṇo bhavati — hence even a broken-rite mantra becomes complete through this placing.
sāñjano 'pi gāruḍavaiṣṇavādir nirañjanatām etya mokṣaprado bhavati — even stained Gāruḍa-Vaiṣṇava and the rest, stainless, becomes release-giving.
inference: Broken and stained mantras completed and purified by her nyāsa.

speaker: Teacher (vessel)
question: What next?
premises: dehanyāsānantaram arghapātre ayam eva nyāsaḥ — after body-placing, this same placing on the vessel.

speaker: Teacher (rite as example)
question: Why is pūjā the example?
premises: iha hi kriyākārakāṇāṃ parameśvarābhedapratipattidārḍhyasiddhaye pūjākriyā udāharaṇīkṛtā — for firmness of Lord-identity realization, the worship-act is made example.
tatra ca sarvakārakāṇām itthaṃ parameśvarībhāvaḥ — there of all factors thus Lord-ness.

tatra yaṣṭrādhārasya sthānaśuddhyāpādānakaraṇayor arghapātraśuddhinyāsābhyām yaṣṭur dehanyāsāt yājyasya sthaṇḍilādinyāsāt — of sacrificer, support, vessel, sacrificer's body, worshippable, altar: each made Lord through its placing.
inference: Every factor made Lord through its placing; worship the example.

speaker: Teacher (seeing the Lord)
question: What follows?
premises: evaṃ kriyākrameṇāpi parameśvarīkṛtasamastakārakaḥ tayaiva dṛśā sarvakriyāḥ paśyan vināpi pramukhajñānayogābhyāṃ parameśvara eva bhavati — thus, all factors Lord-made, seeing all rites with just this view, without chief knowledge and yoga, one becomes the Supreme Lord.
inference: Seeing all factors as Lord = becoming Lord, no yoga needed.

speaker: Teacher (sprinkling)
question: How close?
premises: evam arghapātre nyasya puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā tadvipruḍbhir yāgasāraṃ puṣpādi ca prokṣayet — on the vessel placed, worshipped, sprinkle rite-essence and flowers with its drops.

speaker: Teacher (retinue)
question: How honor the retinue?
premises: tataḥ prabhāmaṇḍale bhūmau khe vā oṃ bāhyaparivārāya nama iti pūjayet — in halo-circle, on ground or in sky: oṃ to the outer retinue, hail.
inference: Halo-circle retinue worship, ground or sky.

speaker: Teacher (door)
question: How enter?
premises: tato dvārasthāne oṃ dvāradevatācakrāya nama iti pūjayet — at the door-place: oṃ to the door-deity-wheel, hail.

speaker: Teacher (outer rite)
question: What if unguarded outside?
premises: agupte tu bahiḥsthāne sati praviśya maṇḍalasthaṇḍilāgra eva bāhyaparivāradevatācakrapūjāṃ pūrvoktaṃ ca nyāsādi kuryāt na bahiḥ — if unguarded outside, having entered: on the maṇḍala-altar-front alone do outer-retinue worship and the aforesaid placing; not outside.

speaker: Teacher (clearing)
question: How clear the way?
premises: tato 'pi phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ iti astrajaptapuṣpaṃ prakṣipya vighnān apasāritān dhyātvā antaḥ praviśya — phaṭ thrice; weapon-muttered flower thrown; obstacles removed meditated; within entered.
parameśvarakiraṇeddhayā dṛṣṭyā abhito yāgagṛhaṃ paśyet — with Lord-ray-kindled gaze see all around the worship-house.

speaker: Teacher (north facing)
question: How stand?
premises: tatra mumukṣur uttarābhimukhas tiṣṭhet — the release-seeker stands facing north.
yathā bhagavadaghoratejasā jhaṭity eva pruṣṭapāśo bhavet — so by the Lord's Aghora-radiance swiftly burnt-bonded he may become.

speaker: Teacher (directions)
question: What are directions?
premises: tatra parameśvarasvātantryam eva mūrtyābhāsanayā diktattvam avabhāsayati — the Lord's freedom alone, by form-shining, shines forth the direction-principle.

speaker: Teacher (middle)
question: What is the middle?
premises: tatra citprakāśa eva madhyaṃ — awareness-light alone the middle.
tata itarapravibhāgapravṛtteḥ — thence other-division arising.
prakāśasvīkāryam ūrdhvam — to be taken as light: above.
atathābhūtam adhaḥ — what is not thus: below.
prakāśanasammukhīnaṃ pūrvam — facing light: east.
itarat aparam — the other: west.
saṃmukhībhūtaprakāśatvāt anantaraṃ tatprakāśadhārārohasthānaṃ dakṣiṇam — from become-facing-light, the next light-stream-rise-place: south.
ānukūlyāt tatsammukhaṃ tu avabhāsyatvāt uttaram — from favour, facing it, but from to-be-shone: north.
iti dikcatuṣkam — thus the direction-four.

speaker: Teacher (Bhairava faces)
question: Who faces where?
premises: tatra madhye bhagavān — in the middle the Lord.
ūrdhve 'sya aiśānaṃ vaktram — above his north-eastern face.
adhaḥ pātālavaktram — below the underworld face.
pūrvādidikcatuṣke śrītatpuruṣāghorasadyovāmākhyaṃ — east-and-rest four: Tatpuruṣa-Aghora-Sadyas-Vāma.
dikcatuṣkamadhye anyāś catasraḥ — in the four-middle the other four.
inference: Bhairava faces: center, above, below, four quarters, four between.

speaker: Teacher (directions truth)
question: Are directions real?
premises: ity evaṃ saṃvinmahimaiva mūrtikṛtaṃ digbhedaṃ bhāsayati — thus awareness-glory alone, formed, shines forth direction-difference.
iti dik na tattvāntaram — thus direction is no other principle.
inference: Directions = awareness-glory formed; no separate principle.

speaker: Teacher (centrality)
question: How is centrality reached?
premises: yathā yathā svacchāyā laṅghayitum iṣṭā satī puraḥ puro bhavati — as the shadow is to be overstepped, being, before, before it becomes.
tathā parameśvaramadhyatām eti — so the Lord's centrality is reached.
sarvaadhiṣṭhātṛtaiva mādhyasthyam — being all-presiding alone is centrality.
ity uktam — thus said.

speaker: Teacher (sun)
question: What of the sun?
premises: evaṃ yathā bhagavān digvibhāgakārī tathā sūryo 'pi — as the Lord divides quarters, so the sun.
sa hi pārameśvary eva jñānaśaktir ity uktaṃ — for it indeed is the Lord's knowledge-power, said.
tatra tatra tatra pūrvaṃ vyakteḥ pūrvā — there, there, there: east of the manifest is east.
yatraiva ca tathā tatraiva — just where, so right there.
evaṃ svātmādhīnāpi svasammukhīnasya deśasya purastāttvāt — self-ruled yet facing-own-place in front.
inference: Sun = Lord's knowledge-power; east wherever manifest; self-ruled yet facing.

speaker: Teacher (threefold one)
question: How are three one?
premises: evaṃ svātmasūryaparameśatritayaikībhāvanayā dikcarcā — by self-sun-Lord-triad-unification: direction-discussion.
iti abhinavaguptaguravaḥ — so Abhinavagupta's gurus.

speaker: Teacher (throne)
question: What follows?
premises: evaṃ sthite uttarābhimukham upaviśya dehapuryaṣṭakādau ahambhāvatyāgena dehatāṃ dahet — standing thus, facing north sit; burning body-ness in body-city-eight by I-feeling abandonment.
saṃnidhāv api paradehavat adehatvāt — near yet as another's body, from bodilessness.
tato nistrāṅgadhruvadhāmarūḍhasya dṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt — then from waveless-steady-abode-mounted, by gaze-nature.
yā kila ādyā spandakalā saiva mūrtiḥ — which indeed is the first throb-digit: that alone is form.
tadupari yathopadiṣṭayājyadevatācakranyāsaḥ — thereupon the as-taught worshippable-deity-wheel-placing.
prādhānyena ca iha śaktayo yājyāḥ — chiefly too here the powers are to be worshipped.
inference: I-feeling burnt; waveless abode; first throb-digit form; wheel-placing with powers chief.

speaker: Teacher (why powers)
question: Why powers chief?
premises: tadāsanatvāt bhagavannavātmādīnāṃ śakter eva ca pūjyatvāt — from that-being-seat, of the Lord-nine-self and the rest; of power alone, from worship-worthiness.
iti guravaḥ — so the gurus.
inference: Seat-ness and power's worthiness: gurus' reason.

speaker: Teacher (states)
question: Which states contemplated?
premises: tatra ca pañca avasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhī ca anuttarā nāma svabhāvadaśā anusaṃdheyā — five states waking and the rest; sixth called unsurpassed, nature-state: to be contemplated.

speaker: Teacher (sixfold seal)
question: How many?
premises: iti ṣoḍhā nyāso bhavati — thus sixfold is the placing.

speaker: Teacher (fullness)
question: What is fullness?
premises: tatra kāraṇānāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivaśaktirūpāṇāṃ pratyekam adhiṣṭhānāt — by each cause's presiding, Brahmā-to-power-formed.
ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakalāpasya laukikatattvottīrṇasya bhairavabhaṭṭārakābhedavṛtte nyāse pūrṇatvāt — of the 36-principle-group, world-transcended, in Bhairava-non-difference-course placing, from fullness.
bhairavībhāvaḥ — Bhairavī-being.
tena etat anavakāśam — hence this has no opening.
inference: Presiding causes; transcended group; fullness = Bhairavī-being; no opening.

speaker: Question (need)
question: What need of more?
premises: yad āhuḥ ataraṅgarūḍhau labdhāyāṃ punaḥ kiṃ tattvasṛṣṭir nyāsādinā iti — which they say: gained in waveless mounting, again what with principle-emission through placing and the rest?
inference: Objection: waveless gained — why more emission-placing?

speaker: Teacher (answer)
question: What answers?
premises: tāvat hi tad ataraṅgaṃ bhairavavapuḥ — so long indeed that waveless Bhairava-formed.
yat svātmani avabhāsitasṛṣṭisaṃhārāvaicitryakoṭi — which in own self shows emission-dissolution-variety-peak.
inference: Answer: waveless Bhairava shows variety-peak in self.

speaker: Teacher (seeing)
question: How see?
premises: evam anyonyamelakayogena parameśvarībhūtaṃ prāṇadehabuddhyādi bhāvayitvā — thus by mutual-meeting-yoga, Lord-made breath-body-mind contemplated.
bahir antaḥ puṣpadhūpatarpaṇādyair yathāsambhavaṃ pūjayet — outside and within, with flowers-smoke-satings as possible, worship.

speaker: Teacher (trident-lotus)
question: How the lotus-seat?
premises: tatra śarīre prāṇe dhiyi ca tadanusāreṇa śūlābjanyāsaṃ kuryāt — in body, breath, mind accordingly do the trident-lotus-placing.
tad yathā ādhāraśaktimūle mūlaṃ kanda āmūlasārakaṃ lambikānte kalātattvāntam daṇḍaḥ — as at base-power-root: root, bulb, to-root-pith, hanging-end, to-kalā-principle-end: the staff.
māyātmako granthiḥ — Māyā-natured knot.
catuṣkikātmā śuddhavidyāpadmaṃ — four-natured pure-knowledge lotus.
tatraiva sadāśivabhaṭṭārakaḥ — right there Lord Sadāśiva.
sa eva mahāpretaḥ — he alone the great corpse.
prakarṣeṇa līnatvāt — through excellence dissolved.
bodhāt — from awakening.
prādhānyena — chiefly.
vedyātmakadehakṣayāt — from knowable-bodied body-decay.
nādāmarśātmakatvāt ca — and from sound-touch-awareness-nature.

speaker: Teacher (inner worship)
question: What is inner worship?
premises: tan nābhyutthitaṃ tanmūrdharandhratrayanirgataṃ nādāntarvartiśaktivyāpinīsamanārūpamarātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ — That risen from the navel, come out of the three head-openings at its top, abiding inside sound, power-pervader, equanimity-formed and the rest, the six-end.
tadupari śuddhapadmatrayam aunmanasam — thereupon the pure lotus-triad, beyond-mind.

etasmin viśvamaye bhede āsanīkṛte adhiṣṭhātṛtayā vyāpakabhāvena ādheyabhūtāṃ yathābhimatāṃ devatāṃ kalpayitvā — on this universe-made division made seat, presiding as pervading-being, the desired become-supported deity having fashioned.
yat tatraiva samasvabhāvanirbharātmani viśvabhāvārpaṇaṃ tad eva pūjanaṃ — which right there, in same-disposition-full self, universe-being-offering: that alone is worship.
yad eva tanmayībhavanaṃ tad dhyānaṃ — which alone becoming-that: that is meditation.
yat tathāvidhāntaḥparāmarśasadbhāvanādāndolanaṃ sa japaḥ — which inner-deliberation-being-shaking as of such: that is murmur.

yat tathāvidhaparāmarśakramaprabuddhamahātejasā tathābalād eva viśvātmīkaraṇaṃ sa homaḥ — which by such-deliberation-order-awakened great-splendour, by that force alone, is universe-self-making: that is oblation.
tad evaṃ kṛtvā parivāraṃ tata eva vahnirāśer visphuliṅgavat dhyātvā tathaiva pūjayet — that done, retinue, from that like sparks from a fire-heap, having meditated, just so worship.
inference: Offering = worship; becoming = meditation; shaking = murmur; universe-self-making = oblation; retinue like sparks.

speaker: Verse (trident)
question: What is the trident?
premises: dvādaśāntam idaṃ prāgraṃ viśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran — remembering this foremost trident, from the root to the twelve-end.
inference: Remember the trident root to twelve-end.
uncertainties: prāgraṃ fork adjudicated (foremost). viśūlaṃ fork adjudicated (trident).

option_choices.reason: trident-foremost fits root-to-twelve-end remembering; eastern-front unmotivated
rite remembers the trident (śūla-nyāsa above); privative sense contradicts

speaker: Verse (going)
question: How go?
premises: devīcakrāgragaṃ tyaktakramaḥ khecaratāṃ vrajet — leaving sequence, going to goddess-wheel-front attains sky-going-ness.

speaker: Verse (filling)
question: What fills?
premises: mūlādhārād dviṣaṭkāntavyomāgrāpūraṇātmikā — from root-support, of twice-six-end-sky-peak-filling nature.

speaker: Verse (living)
question: On what live?
premises: khecarīyaṃ khasaṃcāramsthibhyāṃ khāmṛtāśanāt — sky-going-ness, from sky-faring-rest and from sky-nectar-eating.

speaker: Teacher (conclusion)
question: What suffices?
premises: evam antaryāgamātrād eva vastutaḥ kṛtakṛtyatā — thus by inner rite alone, in reality, done-what-was-to-be-done.

speaker: Teacher (outer need)
question: Why outer too?
premises: satyataḥ tadāviṣṭasya tathāpi bahir api kāryo yāgo 'vacchedahānaya eva — truly for the then-entered, still outer is to be done, to remove limitation alone.
yo 'pi tathā samāveśabhāk na bhavati tasya mukhyo bahiryāgaḥ — who too does not partake immersion: his chief is the outer rite.
tadabhyāsāt samāveśalābho — from its practice, immersion-gain.
yatas tasyāpi tu paśutātirodhānāyāntaryāgaḥ — since for him too, to veil beasthood: inner rite.
tadarūḍhāv api tatsaṃkalpabalasya śuddhipradatvāt — when mounted on that too, his resolve-force is purity-giving.
inference: Outer removes limitation and wins immersion; inner veils beasthood and purifies resolve.

speaker: Teacher (preparation)
question: What now?
premises: atha yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣet tadādhivāsanārthaṃ bhūmiparigrahaṃ gaṇeśārcanaṃ kumbhakalaśayoḥ pūjāṃ sthaṇḍilārcanaṃ havanaṃ ca kuryāt — when one wishes initiation, then for preparation: ground-taking, Gaṇeśa-worship, jar-vessel worship, altar-worship, oblation.
inference: Preparation list: ground, Gaṇeśa, vessels, altar, fire.

speaker: Daily rite
question: What of daily?
premises: nityanaimittikos tu sthaṇḍilādyarcanahavane eva — but in daily-and-occasional: altar-and-rest worship-oblation alone.

speaker: Teacher (adhivāsa defined)
question: What is adhivāsa?
premises: tatra adhivāsanaṃ śiṣyasya saṃskṛtayogyatādhānam — preparation: the disciple's refined-fitness-placing.
amblīkaraṇam iva dantānāṃ — like sharpening of teeth.
devasya kartavyonmukhatvagrāhaṇam — the God's taking of toward-work-upturness.
guros tadgrahaṇam — the guru's taking of that.
inference: Adhivāsa: disciple sharpened, God turned, guru taking up.

speaker: Teacher (things)
question: What of things?
premises: upakaraṇadravyāṇāṃ yāgagṛhāntarvartitayā parameśatejobṛṃhaṇena pūjopakaraṇayogyatārpaṇam — of implement-things, being inside the worship-house, through Lord-radiance-swelling: worship-implement-fitness bestowing.

speaker: Teacher (assembly)
question: How assemble?
premises: tatra sarvopakaraṇapūrṇaṃ yāgagṛhaṃ vidhāya bhagavatīṃ mālinīṃ mātṛkāṃ vā smṛtvā — having arranged the all-implement worship-house, remembered the Goddess Mālinī or Mātṛkā.
tadvarṇatejaḥpuñjabharitaṃ gṛhītaṃ bhāvayan — bearing the taken, full of her-letter-radiance-mass.
puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipet — cast the flower-handful.
inference: Arranged house; remembered Goddess; radiance-mass borne; handful cast.

speaker: Teacher (ground-taking)
question: How take ground?
premises: tata uktāstrajaptāni yathāsambhavaṃ siddhārthadhānyākṣatalājādīni tejorūpāṇi vikīrya — stated weapon-muttered mustard-grain-parched-rice, radiance-formed, scattered as possible.
aiśānyāṃ diśi krameṇa saṃghaṭṭayet — gather in order in the north-east.
iti bhūparigrahaḥ — thus ground-taking.
inference: Scattered mustard gathered north-east: ground taken.

speaker: Teacher (jar)
question: How the jar?
premises: tataḥ śuddhavidyāntam āsanaṃ dattvā gaṇapateḥ pūjā — pure-knowledge-end seat given; Gaṇeśa worshipped.
tataḥ kumbham ānandadravyapūritam alaṃkṛtaṃ pūjayet — jar filled with bliss-substance, adorned, worshipped.
tato yājyam anu pūgaṃ nyasya — then the worshippable next, betel placed.
tatra mukhyaṃ mantraṃ sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtayā vidhipūrvakatvena smaran — there the chief mantra, as all-presiding, remembering with rule-precedence.
aṣṭottaraśatamantritaṃ tena taṃ kumbhaṃ kuryāt — with that 108-muttered, make that jar.
inference: Seat, Gaṇeśa, bliss-jar, betel, chief mantra remembered; 108-muttered jar made.

option_choices.reason: betel placed as offering fits rite; multitude unmotivated

speaker: Teacher (second vessel)
question: What of the second?
premises: dvitīyakalaśe vighnaśamanāya astraṃ yajet — in the second vessel, weapons for obstacle-quelling worship.

speaker: Teacher (guardians)
question: Who guards?
premises: tataḥ svasvadikṣu lokapālān sāstrān pūjayet — in own directions worship the weaponed world-guardians.

speaker: Teacher (handing)
question: What handed?
premises: tataḥ śiṣyasya prāk dīkṣitasya haste astrakalaśaṃ dadyāt — to the before-initiated disciple's hand give the weapon-vessel.

speaker: Teacher (guru's jar)
question: What does the guru take?
premises: svayaṃ ca guruḥ kumbham ādadīta — oneself the guru takes the jar.

speaker: Teacher (procession)
question: How process?
premises: tataḥ śiṣyaṃ gṛhaparyanteṣu vighnaśamanāya dhārāṃ pātayantaṃ sakumbho 'nugacchet — making the disciple pour the stream around the house, with jar follow him.
imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhan — reciting this mantra.
bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye — O O Indra! by you in your own direction for obstacle-pacifying.
inference: Disciple pours around; guru follows with Indra verse.

speaker: Teacher (attentiveness)
question: How behave?
premises: sāvadhānena karmāntaṃ bhavitavyaṃ śivājñayā — with attentiveness, to be done to rite's end, by Śiva's command.
inference: Attentive to the end, by Śiva's command.

speaker: Teacher (name)
question: What name?
premises: tryakṣare nāmni bho ity ekam eva — in the three-syllabled name, 'bho' is one alone.
inference: 'Bho' is one in the three-syllabled name.

speaker: Teacher (placing)
question: Where place?
premises: tata aiśānyāṃ diśi kumbhaṃ sthāpayet — then in the north-east direction place the jar.

speaker: Teacher (sprinkling)
question: What over?
premises: vikiropari astrakalaśam — upon the scattered, the weapon-vessel.

speaker: Teacher (both)
question: What both?
premises: tata ubhayapūjanam — then worship of both.

speaker: Teacher (center)
question: What at center?
premises: tataḥ sthaṇḍilamadhye parameśapūjanam — then in the altar-middle Supreme-worship.

speaker: Teacher (fire)
question: How the fire?
premises: tataḥ agnikuṇḍaṃ parameśvaraśaktirūpatayā bhāvayitvā — fire-pit as Supreme-power-formed contemplated.
tatra agniṃ prajvālya hṛdayāntarbodhāgninā saha ekīkṛtya mantraparāmarśasāhityena — fire kindled there, unified with heart-inner-awakening-fire, with mantra-deliberation.
jvalantaṃ śivāgniṃ bhāvayitvā — blazing Śiva-fire contemplated.
tatra nyasya abhyarcya mantrān tarpayet ājyena tilaiś ca — placed, worshipped there; sate mantras with ghee and sesame.
inference: Fire-pit as power; heart-fire unified; mantras sated with ghee-sesame.

speaker: Teacher (refining)
question: How refine?
premises: arghapātreṇa ca prokṣaṇam eva tilājyādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ — and with the vessel, sprinkling alone is sesame-ghee refining.

speaker: Teacher (ladle-spoon)
question: How refine them?
premises: sruksruvayoś ca parameśābhedadṛṣṭir eva hi saṃskāraḥ — and of ladle-and-spoon, non-difference-view alone indeed is refining.

speaker: Teacher (full oblation)
question: How the full oblation?
premises: tato yathāśakti hutvā sruksruvau ūrdhvādhomukhatayā śaktiśivarūpau parasparonmukhau vidhāya — offered as able; ladle-spoon up-down-facing as power-Śiva-formed, mutually facing arranged.

samapādotthito dvādaśāntagaganoditaśivapūrṇacandraniḥsṛtapatatparāmṛtadhārābhāvanāṃ kurvan — standing even-footed, contemplating the stream of supreme nectar fallen, risen in the sky of the twelve-end, risen full-Śiva-moon.
vauṣaḍantaṃ mantram uccārayan ca — and uttering the vauṣaḍ-ending mantra.
ājyakṣayāntaṃ tiṣṭhet — until ghee's end stand.
iti pūrṇāhutiḥ mantracakrasaṃtarpaṇī — full oblation, mantra-wheel-sating.
inference: Even-footed, nectar-stream contemplated, vauṣaḍ uttered till ghee ends.

speaker: Teacher (caru)
question: How share caru?
premises: tataś caruṃ prokṣitam ānīya sthaṇḍilakalaśakumbhavahniṣu bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedya ekabhāgam avaśeṣya śiṣyāya bhāgaṃ dadyāt — sprinkled caru brought; on altar-vessel-jar-fires share by share offered; one share left; to the disciple give a share.
inference: Shared caru; one share left; disciple's share given.

speaker: Teacher (tooth-stick)
question: What next?
premises: tato dantakāṣṭham — then the tooth-stick.

speaker: Teacher (omen)
question: What of the throw?
premises: tatpāto 'gniyamanirṛtidikṣu adhaś ca na śubha iti — its falling in fire-Yama-Nirṛti directions and below is not auspicious: thus.

speaker: Teacher (oblation)
question: What oblation?
premises: tatra homo 'stramantreṇa kāryaḥ — there oblation by weapon-mantra is to be done.

speaker: Teacher (blindfold)
question: How bring in?
premises: tato vikṣepaparihāreṇa bhāvimantradarśanayogyatāyai baddhanetraṃ śiṣyaṃ praveśya — for distraction-avoidance, for fitness to see the future mantra, having brought in the blindfolded disciple.
jānusthitaṃ taṃ kṛtvā puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣepayet — having made him kneeling, have him cast a flower-handful.

speaker: Teacher (sight)
question: What on unveiling?
premises: tataḥ sahasā apāsitanetrabandho 'sau śaktipātānugṛhītakaraṇatvāt — suddenly unfastened-eye-bound, through descent-graced instrument-ness.
saṃnihitamantraṃ tatsthānaṃ sākṣātkāreṇa paśyan tanmayo bhavati — seeing the present mantra in that place face-to-face, becomes made of that.
anugṛhītakaraṇānāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ — of graced instruments mantra-nearness is visible.
yatas trasyatām iva bhūtānām — since as it were of trembling beings.
inference: Unveiled seeing makes one of that; mantra-nearness visible to graced.

speaker: Teacher (bonds)
question: How burn bonds?
premises: tataḥ svadakṣiṇahaste dīpyatayā devatācakraṃ pūjayitvā — in one's own right hand with blazing, having worshipped the deity-wheel.
taṃ hastaṃ mūrdhahṛnnābhiṣu śiṣyasya pāśān dahantaṃ nikṣipet — placing it burning the disciple's bonds on head-heart-navel.
inference: Blazing right hand burns head-heart-navel bonds.

speaker: Teacher (left hand)
question: What with the left?
premises: tato vāme somyatayā pūjayitvā śuddhatattvāpyāyinaṃ — then in the left with gentleness, having worshipped, fattening with pure principle.
tataḥ praṇāmaṃ kuryāt — then bow.
inference: Gentle left fattens with pure principle; then bow.

speaker: Teacher (offering out)
question: What outside?
premises: tato bhūtadevatādigbaliṃ madyamāṃsajalādipūrṇaṃ bahir dadyāt — being-deity-direction-offering, full of wine-meat-water, outside give.
ācāmeta — having sipped.

speaker: Teacher (staying)
question: How stay?
premises: tataḥ svayaṃ carubhojanaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyātmanā saha aikyam āpannaḥ prabuddhavṛttiḥ tiṣṭhet — having eaten the oblation-meal oneself, with disciple-self attaining oneness, awakened-natured stay.
inference: Meal eaten; oneness with disciple; awakened stay.

speaker: Teacher (dreams)
question: What of dreams?
premises: svapan api prabhāte śiṣyaḥ cet aśubhaṃ svapnaṃ vadet — dreaming too, at dawn if the disciple tells an inauspicious dream.
tat asmai na vyākuryāt — that to him one should not explain.

speaker: Teacher (fear)
question: What of fear?
premises: śaṅkātaṅkau hi tathāsya syātām — doubt and fear would be his.
kevalam astreṇa tanniṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt — merely with the weapon make its expiation.
inference: Unexplained dreams breed fear; weapon-expiation only.

speaker: Teacher (entering)
question: How enter the disciple?
premises: tatas tathaiva parameśvaraṃ pūjayitvā tadagre śiṣyasya prāṇakrameṇa praviśya — just so worshipped the Lord, entered before him by the disciple's breath-course.
hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu ṣaṭsu kāraṇaṣaṭkasparśaṃ kurvan — in heart-throat-palate-brow-cleft-twelve-ends, six six-cause-touchings doing.
pratyekam aṣṭau saṃskārān cintayan — each eight refinements contemplating.
kaṃcit kālaṃ śiṣyaprāṇaṃ tatraiva viśramayya — some time resting the disciple-breath right there.
punar avarohet — again descend.
inference: Breath-course entry; six places touched; eight refinements each; rest; descend.

speaker: Teacher (samayin)
question: What results?
premises: ity evāpāditāṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskāroparikṛtarudrāṃśāpattiḥ samayībhavati — thus effected-forty-eight-refinements-upon-made-Rudra-part-attainment becomes a samayin.

speaker: Teacher (mantra gift)
question: What bestowed?
premises: tataḥ asmai pūjyaṃ mantraṃ puṣpādyaiḥ saha arpayet — then to him the worshippable mantra with flowers and the rest bestow.

speaker: Teacher (rules)
question: What next?
premises: tataḥ samayān asmai nirūpayet — then the rules to him lay down.

speaker: Teacher (samaya code)
question: What are the rules?
premises: gurau sarvātmanā bhaktiḥ — in the guru with whole self, devotion.
tathā śāstre deve tatpratidvaṃdvini parāṅmukhatā — so in scripture; in God; aversion toward their opponents.
guruvat guruputrādeḥ — like the guru, of the guru's son and the rest.
vidyāsambandhakṛtasya tatpūrvadīkṣitādeḥ saṃdarśanam — of the knowledge-tied made, of the before-initiated and the rest, seeing.
yaunasambandhasya tadārādhanārtham na tu svata — of the womb-tie, for its honouring, not by oneself.
iti mantavyam — thus to be deemed.
inference: Devotion to guru/scripture/God; aversion to opponents; reverence to kin and fellow-initiates.

speaker: Teacher (women)
question: What of women?
premises: striyo vandhyāyās tajjugupsāhetuṃ na kuryāt — of women, of the barren that-loathing-cause one should not do.
uncertainties: tajjugupsāhetuṃ formation obscure; reading follows print.

speaker: Teacher (names)
question: What of names?
premises: devatānāma gurunāma tathā mantraṃ pūjākālāt ṛte na uccārayet — deity-name, guru-name, and mantra, apart from worship-time, one should not utter.

speaker: Teacher (guru's things)
question: What of the guru's things?
premises: gurūpabhuktaṃ śayyādi na bhuñjīta — what the guru has enjoyed — bed and the rest — one should not enjoy.
inference: Guru-enjoyed things not to be enjoyed.

speaker: Teacher (play)
question: What of play?
premises: yat kiṃcit laukikaṃ krīḍādi tat gurusaṃnidhau na kuryāt — what games and the rest are worldly, that in the guru's nearness one should not do.
inference: No worldly play near the guru.

speaker: Teacher (excellence)
question: What of excellence?
premises: tadvyatirekeṇa na anyatra utkarṣabuddhiṃ kuryāt — apart from that, elsewhere one should not make excellence-thought.

speaker: Teacher (worship)
question: Whom worship?
premises: sarvatra śrāddhādau gurum eva pūjayet — everywhere, in śrāddha and the rest, the guru alone worship.

speaker: Teacher (speech)
question: What not say?
premises: sarveṣu ca naimittikeṣu śākinītyādiśabdān na vadet — and in all occasionals, śākinī-and-the-rest words one should not say.

speaker: Teacher (festivals)
question: What of festivals?
premises: parvadināni pūjayet — festival days worship.

speaker: Teacher (company)
question: Whose company?
premises: vaiṣṇavādyair adhodṛṣṭibhiḥ saha saṃgatiṃ na kuryāt — with those of lower sight, Vaiṣṇavas and the rest, company one should not make.

speaker: Teacher (birth)
question: What of birth?
premises: etacchāsanasthān pūrvajātibuddhyā na paśyet — abiding in this teaching, one should not see with former-birth thought.
inference: No former-birth thought in this teaching.

speaker: Teacher (hospitality)
question: What hospitality?
premises: guruvarge gṛhāgate yathāśakti yāgaṃ kuryāt — when the guru's circle has come home, as able do worship.
inference: Worship as able for the guru's circle.

speaker: Teacher (apostates)
question: What of apostates?
premises: adhomārgasthitaṃ kaṃcit vaiṣṇavādyaṃ tacchāstrakulāt gurūkṛtyāpi tyajet — a lower-path abider, having even made him guru, from his teaching-clan abandon.
inference: Abandon even a guru-turned-apostate with his clan.

speaker: Teacher (seeing)
question: How see them?
premises: tadāpi na utkarṣabuddhyā paśyet — even then one should not see with excellence-thought.

speaker: Teacher (sects)
question: What of sects?
premises: liṅgibhiḥ saha samācāramelanaṃ na kuryāt — with mark-bearers no conduct-meeting make.
tān kevalaṃ yathāśakti pūjayet — them only as able worship.
inference: No mixing with sects; mere as-able worship.

speaker: Teacher (doubt)
question: What of doubt?
premises: śaṅkās tyajet — doubts abandon.

speaker: Teacher (divisions)
question: What of divisions?
premises: cakre sthitaś caramāgryādivibhāgaṃ janmakṛtaṃ na saṃkalpayet — in the wheel, standing, of last-and-first division, birth-made, one should not fancy.
inference: No birth-made last-first fancy in the wheel.

speaker: Teacher (holy places)
question: What of holy places?
premises: śarīrāt ṛte na anyat āyatanatīrthādikaṃ bahumānena paśyet — apart from the body, no other abode-ford and the rest with high regard see.
inference: No abode higher than the body.

speaker: Teacher (dakṣiṇā)
question: What giving?
premises: mantrahṛdayam anavarataṃ smaret — constantly remember the mantra-heart.

ity evaṃ śiṣyaḥ śrutvā praṇamya abhyupagamya guruṃ dhanadāraśarīraparyantayā dakṣiṇayā paritoṣya — thus the disciple, having heard, bowed, accepted, the guru with wealth-wife-body-up-to gift pleasing.
pūrvadīkṣitāṃś ca dīnānāthādikān tarpayet — and the before-initiated and poor-lordless sating.
inference: Constant mantra-heart; wealth-to-body dakṣiṇā; sating of priors and poor.

speaker: Teacher (image)
question: What image rite?
premises: bhāvividhinā ca mūrticakraṃ tarpayet — and with the future rule, the image-wheel sate.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What is he?
premises: itthaṃ samayībhavati — thus one becomes a samayin.
inference: Thus samayin: seal of the ahnika.

speaker: Teacher (entitlement)
question: What entitlement?
premises: mantrābhyāse nityapūjāyāṃ śravaṇe 'dhyayane adhikārī — in mantra-practice, daily worship, hearing, study: entitled.
naimittike tu sarvatra gurum eva abhyarthayet — but in the occasional, everywhere the guru alone request.
inference: Entitled to practice/study; occasionals need the guru.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What rule?
premises: iti sāmayiko vidhiḥ — thus the samayin rule.
